tools.description:

- Link: [New Document](https://example.com/doc/abc123)

⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='google_docs_smart_create_from_markdown', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

CRITICAL: DO NOT include emojis in the markdown_content parameter. Use plain text only. Emojis cause formatting errors and encoding issues.

SMART TOOL: Create fully formatted Google Docs from markdown. HEADING HIERARCHY: H1-H3 (####) for document structure, H4 (####) ONLY titles above paragraphs and titles of nummbered or bulleted lists (11pt bold). Supports: # headings (H1-H6, always black), **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, ==highlight==, `code`, ```blocks```, [links](url), ![images](url), nested bullets/numbers (indent 2 spaces), > blockquotes, --- lines, <<NEW-PAGE>>, <<BOOKMARK:name>> (creates named range for navigation), TEXT ALIGNMENT: <text< (left), >text< (center), >text> (right), and | tables |. Use H4 directly above bulleted/numbered lists.

BOOKMARK SYNTAX: <<BOOKMARK:section_name>> creates a named range that can be linked directly: document_url#bookmark=section_name. Use for table of contents, section navigation, or external references.

SMART TOOL v2.0 (ENHANCED): Create Google Docs from markdown using DOCX conversion with FULL FORMATTING (30+ features). Default font: Arial 11pt (matching Google Docs default - NOT Times New Roman). Faster than API method, much less code, high success rate. Uses python-docx and Drive auto-conversion.

DEFAULT FONT: Arial 11pt (matches Google Docs, NOT Times New Roman)
HEADING SIZES: H1=20pt, H2=18pt, H3=16pt, H4-H6=11pt (matches Smart V1)

COMPLETE MARKDOWN SUPPORT:

TEXT FORMATTING:
- **bold** or __bold__ -> Bold text
- *italic* or _italic_ -> Italic text
- __underline__ -> Underlined text (double underscore)
- ~~strikethrough~~ -> Strikethrough text
- ==highlight== -> Yellow highlighted text
- `inline code` -> Monospace code
- H~2~O -> Subscript (H2O)
- x^2^ -> Superscript (x2)

STRUCTURE:
- # to ###### -> 6 heading levels (H1-H6)
- - or * -> Bullet lists
- 1. 2. 3. -> Numbered lists
-   - (2 spaces) -> Nested lists (unlimited levels)
- | Tables | -> Professional tables
- ```code blocks``` -> Monospace code blocks
- > Blockquotes -> Indented quotes

SPECIAL ELEMENTS:
- --- or *** -> Horizontal line
- <<PAGE-BREAK>> or <<< -> Page break
- <<BOOKMARK:name>> -> Create Word bookmark for navigation
- <<TOC>> -> Auto-generate table of contents (update in Word)
- ![alt](url) -> Images from URLs
- [Link](url) -> Hyperlinks

NAVIGATION FEATURES:
- Bookmarks: <<BOOKMARK:section_name>> creates Word bookmark
- TOC: <<TOC>> generates table of contents from headings (requires Word to update page numbers)

ALIGNMENT:
- ->centered text<- -> Center aligned
- <-left text -> Left aligned
- right text-> -> Right aligned

ADVANTAGES OVER V1:
- Faster (0.5-2s vs 2-8s)
- Much less code
- High success rate
- Automatic shareability
- Simpler to use and debug

AUTO-SHAREABLE: Documents automatically shareable with edit permissions.

Complementary to v1 (API-based) - both tools available.

tools.description:
🚨 CRITICAL EXECUTION RULES:

(2) MUST cite resource: 'Read X from **[Resource Name]** (ID: `[id]` | URL: [url])'

Example response:
Read 45 rows from **Sales Spreadsheet**
- ID: `xyz789`
- URL: https://example.com/sheet/xyz789
- Data: [actual data read]

⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='google_docs_get_document', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

🔄 UPDATED (Nov 2025): Default format changed to 'summary' to prevent token overflow.

Get document content with format control to prevent Claude 200K token limit errors.

FORMAT OPTIONS:
- 'summary' (DEFAULT): Returns title + first 2000 characters preview + metadata
  • Prevents token overflow (reduces 200K+ tokens to ~500 tokens)
  • Perfect for checking document existence, title, or preview
  • Use this first, then use google_docs_search_document() for specific sections

- 'text': Returns complete document as plain text (no formatting metadata)
  • 90% token reduction vs 'full' format
  • Good for documents under 50K tokens
  • Still may hit limits on very large documents

- 'markdown': Returns formatted document with headings, bold, italic, lists
  • 85% token reduction vs 'full' format
  • Preserves structure while removing JSON metadata
  • Good for documents under 50K tokens

- 'full': Complete JSON with all formatting (LEGACY - NOT RECOMMENDED)
  • Can be 200K+ tokens for large documents
  • Will trigger 'prompt too long' errors on documents >100 pages
  • Only use for small documents (<10 pages)

RECOMMENDED WORKFLOW FOR LARGE DOCUMENTS:
1. Call with format='summary' to check title and preview (500 tokens)
2. Use google_docs_search_document(query='...') to find relevant sections (2K tokens)
3. Only use format='text' or 'markdown' if document is small (<50 pages)

Example response (format='summary'):
{
  'success': True,
  'title': 'Annual Report 2024',
  'document_id': '1M11p3S...',
  'preview': 'Executive Summary\nOur company achieved...', 
  'preview_length': 2000,
  'format': 'summary',
  'note': 'Showing first 2000 chars. Use format="text" for full content or google_docs_search_document() for specific sections.'
}

WARNING: The document '1M11p3SwvTHFSF5pcJd-oq2w9E_ShaBL17IMckkpkvj0' triggered a 400 error with 209,727 tokens (>200K limit) when using format='full'. Always use format='summary' or google_docs_search_document() for large documents.

format.description: Output format: 'summary' (DEFAULT - 2K preview), 'text' (plain text), 'markdown' (formatted), 'full' (complete JSON - NOT RECOMMENDED)

returns.description: Document content in requested format (default: summary with 2000 char preview)

🆕 NEW TOOL (Nov 2025): Search document for specific text and return only matching sections.

EXTREMELY token-efficient for large documents (90%+ reduction):
- Returns ONLY sections matching your query with surrounding context
- Perfect for Q&A: "What does the document say about X?"
- Perfect for extraction: "Find all mentions of Y"
- Prevents 200K+ token responses that cause 400 errors

USE THIS INSTEAD OF google_docs_get_document when:
- Document is large (>50 pages) 
- You need specific information (not entire document)
- Previous google_docs_get_document calls caused token overflow
- You want to ask questions about document content

Example response:

  'success': True,
  'title': 'Product Manual',
  'document_id': '1M11p3S...',
  'query': 'warranty',
  'match_count': 3,
  'showing': 3,
  'matches': [
    {
      'text': '...warranty coverage includes manufacturing defects and material failures for a period of 12 months...',
      'position': 1520,
      'context_length': 800,
      'match_number': 1
    },
    {
      'text': '...extended warranty plans are available for purchase separately...',
      'position': 4890,
      'context_length': 800,
      'match_number': 2
    }
  ],
  'note': 'Found 3 matches, showing 3 with 800 chars context each'
}

Common use cases:
- 'Find sections about clinical competence' → Returns relevant paragraphs
- 'What does it say about assessment?' → Extracts assessment-related content
- 'Search for Year 2 transition' → Finds transition information
- 'Look for self-scoring' → Returns scoring-related sections
